big_case.notes: Emergency-docket stay of a sector-wide injunction halting border-barrier construction across the Big Bend Sector, resolved by a signed-off per curiam (one noted dissent) holding there is no such thing as a constitutional major-questions claim for purposes of IIRIRA 102(c)(2)(A)'s review bar. Real national policy and environmental stakes and a doctrinal statement with reach beyond the case, but an interim order on a narrow jurisdictional question rather than a merits landmark.

leakage.notes: Forward cell (log mode forward; prediction created 2026-10-23, outcome resolved 2026-11-09). Log calls are all result-unobserved; graded on queries. Queries reached the open corpus row for 26A560 (showing the Oct 22 response request, disclosed in reasoning), the W.D. Tex. docket (ECF 75/77/78, all dated on or before Oct 21), and resolved priors. The Oct 22 response request is post-anchor but is legitimate forward signal on a genuinely open case. Nothing dated on or after the Nov 9 resolution, no read of data/qp-topics.

central_claims.basis: Nov 9 order: application referred to the Court is granted; injunction stayed pending filing and disposition of the Government's cert petition; no summary reversal.
central_claims.claim: The Court will enter an unqualified grant of the stay pending the filing and disposition of a cert petition, in standard interim form, not cert before judgment or summary reversal.

central_claims.basis: Per curiam: 'There is no such thing as a "constitutional" major-questions claim'; respondents' claim alleges the Secretary exceeded statutory authority (Dalton v. Specter).
central_claims.claim: The ground: the major-questions doctrine is a canon of statutory interpretation, not a standalone constitutional claim that can overcome 102(c)(2)(A)'s bar.

central_claims.basis: The per curiam's equities rest on IIRIRA 102(c)(1)'s congressional balance, Von Raab, NIH v. APHA and Winter; it does not invoke CASA overbreadth or Sierra Club. Equities did favor the government, so this held only in direction.
central_claims.claim: Overbreadth under Trump v. CASA and equities per Sierra Club/NPS v. National Trust favor the government.

central_claims.basis: Only Justice Jackson is noted as would deny.
central_claims.claim: Vote 6-3, with Sotomayor, Kagan and Jackson voting to deny and likely noting dissents.
Disposition within roughly 7 to 14 days of the Oct 21 filing (late Oct / early Nov).
